hints: Sort the suffixes and look at their prefixes.
A suffix adds one new substring for every length greater than its LCP with the previous suffix.
Add one to a whole interval of lengths using a difference array.
analogy: Each suffix contributes a consecutive range of substring lengths, like adding one to all boxes on a shelf.
example: For aba, there are 2 distinct substrings of length 1, 2 of length 2, and 1 of length 3.
algorithm: Build the suffix array and adjacent LCP array. For each suffix of length len and previous LCP l, add one to all lengths l+1 through len using difference-array endpoints. Prefix-sum the difference array and print the count for each length 1 through n.
correctness: A suffix's prefixes of lengths at most l appeared earlier, and all longer prefixes are new. These intervals partition the distinct substrings by their first suffix in sorted order, so summing them gives each length's exact count.
complexity: For length n, O(n log n) time using a doubling suffix array and O(n) space.
